subject: SLA uplift credit addendum + escalation runbook discussion
messages:
From: Alex Mosley <alex@brightcart.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA uplift & escalation coverage for BrightCart renewal

Evelyn / team,

Hope you’re well. Our renewal for BrightCart (term starts 2026-11-01) is coming up and we need to firm up SLA terms before procurement signs off. Two asks from our side:

- Credits: we are looking for a small uptime credit buffer if availability drops below 99.9% (we run mission-critical checkout flows). Can you outline a credit schedule tied to uptime bands?
- Escalation runbook: we need a short, named escalation flow (hours-of-coverage, SLAs for Tier 1 triage, and a single named Redwood on-call contact during weekends). Procurement also wants the addendum text to drop into our SOW for DocuSign.

High level constraints: we won’t expand commit unless we have predictable economics (credits help). Renewal value expected to be ~ $420k ARR.

Can you send a draft addendum + proposed credit matrix this week?

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Mosley
Head of Infrastructure
BrightCart

---
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mosley <alex@brightcart.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@brightcart.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA uplift & escalation coverage for BrightCart renewal

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a short draft addendum and an escalation runbook (attachment stubs below). Key proposal summary:

- Uptime credit schedule (applies per month):
  * >= 99.95%: no credits
  * 99.9% - 99.95%: 5% monthly credit
  * 99.0% - 99.9%: 15% monthly credit
  * < 99.0%: 40% of that month’s invoice (capped at 100% for severe outages)

- Response & escalation coverage:
  * Business hours (Mon–Fri 08:00–20:00 PT): 2hr initial response, 6hr mitigation update cadence
  * Off-hours & weekends: 4hr initial response, named on-call escalation.
  * Critical SEV1 triage: immediate pager to on-call SRE + priority channel to engineering lead.

- Named escalation contact for weekends: Jordan Blake (product ops) — we’ll include a dedicated pager/phone line in the runbook.

- Credits are invoiced as a credit memo applied to the next monthly invoice; if BrightCart signs a 12-month commit > $500k ARR we can bump the first two credit tiers by 2pp (e.g., reduce the 15% band to 13%).

Attachments: redwood-sla-addendum-draft.pdf (PDF, 142KB), escalation_runbook_v2.docx (Docx, 76KB)

If that looks reasonable I’ll route the addendum to Contracts for a tracked redline and prep a DocuSign envelope.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0123

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: internal: BrightCart addendum — suggested edits

Eve / Jordan — quick internal notes on the draft before we send to Contracts / Alex: 

- Weekend named contact: Jordan is fine, but procurement may request a titled contact ("Escalation Lead: Jordan Blake, Sr. Product Ops") and a backup. Add a 2nd named backup (I suggest Marissa Cole as backup).
- Credits: move to a monthly rolling lookback rather than a single-month cap (this protects both sides). Suggest language: "Credits are calculated on a rolling 30-day window and applied as a credit memo to the next invoice."
- DocuSign flow: procurement usually requires a single combined SOW + addendum envelope. We should prepare an insertion-ready clause instead of a separate PDF.
- Optional concession ask: if BrightCart expands to > $600k ARR within the first 90 days of renewal, offer an up-front 1-month free of Premium Support (not credit) to accelerate commit.

I’ve highlighted the lines in the docx. Once you approve I’ll loop in Contracts and Sales Ops for the envelope and HubSpot update.

-V
Vanessa Ortiz
VP, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference
